subject: paediatrics
title: Apnoea of Prematurity, Caffeine and Diaphragmatic Hernia

steps.tx: Cessation of breathing for twenty seconds or more, or for a shorter duration when accompanied by bradycardia below one hundred beats per minute or cyanosis, defines **apnoea of prematurity**. Directly proportional to the degree of prematurity, it affects almost all infants born before twenty-eight weeks, resolving spontaneously as brainstem respiratory control centers mature.
steps.say: Apnoea of prematurity is a cessation of breathing for twenty seconds or with bradycardia and desaturation.

rows: Central pause followed by obstructed efforts

steps.tx: The underlying pathogenesis involves **brainstem respiratory center immaturity**. Immature medullary chemoreceptors exhibit blunted sensitivity to carbon dioxide and paradoxical respiratory depression in response to hypoxia. Furthermore, highly compliant cartilaginous chest walls, weak diaphragmatic musculature, and collapsible pharyngeal soft tissues predispose premature neonates to obstructive and mixed apnoeic pauses.
steps.say: Blunted chemoreceptor sensitivity and collapsible pharyngeal tissues cause recurrent apnoea.

steps.tx: The pharmacological cornerstone of therapy is the methylxanthine derivative **caffeine citrate therapy**. Administered with an intravenous or oral loading dose of twenty milligrams per kilogram followed by a daily maintenance dose of five to ten milligrams per kilogram, caffeine acts as a competitive antagonist at central adenosine A1 and A2A receptors, stimulating medullary respiratory centers.
steps.say: Caffeine citrate blocks central adenosine receptors to stimulate medullary respiratory drive.

rows: Wide therapeutic window, rarely requires levels

steps.tx: Caffeine wakes the breathing centre by removing a chemical brake. Adenosine normally settles onto A1 and A2A receptors on medullary respiratory neurons and damps their firing, an effect exaggerated in the preterm brain. By occupying those receptors without activating them, **caffeine antagonism** restores carbon dioxide sensitivity and diaphragmatic drive, which is why a daily dose quietly reduces apnoeic pauses and ventilator days.
steps.say: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the medulla, removing a brake on breathing. Carbon dioxide sensitivity and diaphragm drive improve, so apnoeic pauses become less frequent.

vis.alt: Receptor diagram of a brainstem respiratory neuron with caffeine molecules occupying adenosine receptors on its surface.
vis.caption: Caffeine blocking adenosine A1 and A2A receptors in the medullary respiratory centre to treat apnoea of prematurity. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Beyond reducing apnoea frequency, randomized trials demonstrate that early caffeine therapy facilitates **successful extubation from mechanical ventilation**. Caffeine enhances diaphragmatic contractility, increases minute ventilation, and improves hypercapnic sensitivity. Long-term follow-up confirms that caffeine therapy significantly reduces the incidence of bronchopulmonary dysplasia and improves neurodevelopmental outcomes at eighteen months.
steps.say: Caffeine improves diaphragmatic contractility, shortens ventilator time, and lowers chronic lung disease.

left.title: Immediate Respiratory Actions
points: Increases central sensitivity to carbon dioxide
Decreases frequency and duration of hypoxic pauses

right.title: Long-Term Proven Benefits
points: Reduces need for surgical patent ductus ligation
Improves cognitive and motor survival at 18 months

steps.tx: Chronic lung injury resulting from mechanical ventilation and oxygen toxicity in very premature infants is designated **bronchopulmonary dysplasia**. Defined as the continued requirement for supplemental oxygen or positive pressure respiratory support at thirty-six weeks postmenstrual age, modern pathology exhibits arrested alveolarization and dysmorphic microvascular development rather than severe airway fibrosis.
steps.say: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia is oxygen dependency at thirty-six weeks postmenstrual age.

rows: Larger preterms exposed to high pressures
Extremely low birth weight infants (<28 weeks)
Severe airway epithelial necrosis, dense fibrosis

steps.tx: A severe congenital anatomical defect causing acute neonatal respiratory failure is **congenital diaphragmatic hernia**. Arising from failure of the pleuroperitoneal membrane to close at eight to ten weeks gestation, over eighty-five percent occur on the posterolateral left side through the foramen of Bochdalek, allowing herniation of abdominal viscera into the thoracic cavity.
steps.say: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia occurs mostly on the left through the foramen of Bochdalek.

left.title: Bochdalek Hernia (Posterolateral)
points: Accounts for 85 to 90 percent of cases
Left-sided in over 85 percent of presentations

right.title: Morgagni Hernia (Anteromedial)
points: Accounts for under 5 to 10 percent of cases

steps.tx: Physical examination in the delivery room reveals a distinctive triad: respiratory distress, a **scaphoid hollow abdomen**, and displaced heart sounds heard best in the right hemithorax. Auscultation over the left thorax reveals absent breath sounds and audible bowel sounds. Compression by herniated viscera in utero causes severe bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia and irreversible muscularization of pulmonary arterioles.
steps.say: The classic presentation includes a scaphoid abdomen, shifted heart sounds, and severe respiratory distress.

rows: Stomach and bowel herniated into chest
Heart sounds loudest at right mid-clavicular line
Chest X-ray showing intrathoracic bowel loops

steps.tx: A critical emergency rule in managing congenital diaphragmatic hernia is that **bag and mask ventilation is strictly contraindicated**. Positive pressure mask ventilation forces air directly into the herniated intrathoracic stomach and bowel, distending them rapidly and worsening mediastinal compression. Resuscitation mandates immediate endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and placement of a wide-bore nasogastric tube.
steps.say: Bag-mask ventilation is strictly contraindicated; immediate endotracheal intubation is mandatory.
